A1.justification: Despite the changed title, both PDFs describe the same membership-privacy study and retain matching experiments and tables. All 21 pages of v1 and 29 pages of v2, including their appendices, support comparison through readable text and rendered figures, tables and equations.

before.justification: v1 reports original LiRA experiments on fine-tuned image classifiers, regression results, DP-budget experiments and sample-level gradient and distance analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains original experiments and adds synthetic simulations, expanded sample-level analyses and FiLM results explicitly attributed to this work in Table A7.

M1.justification: v2 changes the main regression response from log10(TPR) to log10(TPR-FPR), retaining the original formulation in Appendix B.2. It also introduces a Gaussian-cluster model with empirical class means and inner-product classification for studying LiRA (Section 4.1). Together these substantially extend the paper's modeling approach.

E1.justification: The six image datasets and ImageNet-21K pretraining coverage remain unchanged. v2 adds a distinct synthetic Gaussian-cluster classification setting in Section 4.1 and Figure 4. The additional FiLM and from-scratch evaluations use retained image domains rather than new image benchmarks.

E2.justification: v2 evaluates the original log(TPR) regression as a simpler alternative to its revised predictor, reporting both formulations in Tables A8 and A9. v1 evaluated only the original formulation. LiRA remains the sole attack; FiLM and from-scratch models are evaluation targets.

E3.justification: v2 replaces average-gradient comparisons over all, last 20 and last five steps with root-sum-squared norms over training deciles and R2-based comparisons. It extends regression evaluation to FPR 0.0001 and 0.00001, adds FiLM and published from-scratch target settings, and removes the DP-budget sweep.

E4.justification: The sample-property study expands from two datasets with ViT-B to all six datasets and both backbones, with revised temporal-gradient sensitivity analyses (Figures 5–7 and Appendix B.5). v2 also adds regression-variant comparisons, coefficient sensitivity across FPR and analyses of simulated LiRA distribution parameters. The earlier DP-budget analysis disappears.

E5.justification: The retained analyses preserve six- and twelve-seed summaries, Clopper-Pearson intervals and OLS uncertainty statistics. The fifteen-seed uncertainty summaries disappear with the deleted DP-budget experiment. The additional regression rows and coefficient-error-bar figure do not establish a new uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: Tables A3–A6 retain their numerical results, but v2 adds simulation, FiLM, external from-scratch and expanded sample-level findings, while removing DP-budget results. At FPR 0.001, the retained log(TPR) variant changes from train/test R2 0.917/0.740 to 0.931/0.782. The new log(TPR-FPR) model reports 0.930/0.790; its different response prevents treating these numbers as a direct same-setting performance improvement.

T1.justification: v2 adds Gaussian and equal-variance assumptions, Lemma 1, Corollary 2, Theorem 3 and Appendix C derivations connecting log(TPR-FPR) to log(S), with asymptotic slope -1/2. These are substantial new theoretical developments. The previously reproduced DP attack bound and its associated derivation discussion are removed.

C1.justification: v2 adds a theoretical explanation of the power law as a core contribution and extends prediction claims to other fine-tuning parameterizations. Its abstract replaces the specific claim about gradients at training's end with a broader predictive-gradient claim, while the contribution list makes training-stage dependence dataset-specific.

C2.justification: v1 generally favors late-training gradients; v2 interprets short segments as often similarly predictive and sometimes favors earlier stages. v2 adds explanations for underestimated from-scratch vulnerability, discusses low-FPR deviations from theory, and explicitly limits conclusions to the tested attack and balanced datasets. These materially refine mechanisms and applicability boundaries.

D1.justification: v2 newly documents Adam, feature caching, gradient recording, dataset versions and licenses, checkpoint/data access instructions, hardware and runtimes. It also states that reproduction code accompanies supplementary material and promises a public release. These are substantial disclosures, not evidence that retained experiments changed optimizer or preprocessing. DP-specific accounting and noise-selection details are removed.

R1.justification: v2 removes the supporting DP-training, transfer-learning and accounting discussion and associated citations, while adding Dong et al. on Gaussian DP and Kingma and Ba on Adam. Carlini and Tobaben results also become validation data. The central positioning relative to LiRA and earlier dataset/sample privacy studies remains.

P1.justification: v2 retitles the paper, merges Background and Methods, integrates the experiment overview into the dataset study, and substantially rewrites and subdivides the sample-level analysis. The contributions, discussion and appendix organization are rebuilt, producing substantial narrative and structural changes beyond the added scientific content.

P2.justification: v2 adopts a different document template and author layout, adds coefficient, simulation and generalization plots, and replaces the small sample-property figure with extensive separate panels. Regression axes and legends change, DP plots disappear, and appendix tables and figures are rearranged, including placing Tables A5 and A6 together.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens the empirical power-law study with an explicit, assumption-limited theoretical account and simulation checks. Broader sample-level evidence supports more qualified gradient conclusions, while external target-model checks clarify generalization limits. Detailed reproducibility disclosures and explicit attack limitations also address important gaps in v1. Removing the DP-budget comparison loses useful context, but the gains in explanation, validation and transparency provide a substantial overall improvement.
